gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a named reviewer has actually run one of these HDMI-over-Cat6 splitter kits at a set distance; The Gadgeteer (David Sheneman, 2023-03-05) ran the IOGEAR GVE4K60KIT at 3840×2160 60p over about 150 ft of Cat6 and it worked. That is 35 ft past the 115 ft 4K60 rating of OREI's 2-TV pick.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited OREI support pages (UHD12-EX115-K and UHD14-EXB400-K) and the other OREI support and orei.com results ChatGPT got. They give only the maker's maximum ratings (115 ft or 394 ft at 4K60, 8.28 W or 35 W). None states a latency figure or any test by a third party at a stated cable length. No named lab (RTINGS, Notebookcheck or a magazine lab) has published measurements for any of the three products ChatGPT showed. The only hands-on run with a stated cable length is The Gadgeteer's IOGEAR test. The only latency figures in milliseconds come from SC&T's own lab report, and SC&T makes extenders.
decides: This adds a fourth candidate rather than deciding the pick. For 2 TVs at 115–150 ft, the IOGEAR GVE4K60KIT ($149.95 at iogear.com) has a named reviewer's working 4K60 run at about 150 ft. The OREI UHD12-EX115-K ($139.99 in ChatGPT's answer) is rated for only 115 ft at 4K60, so it does not cover that distance. SC&T measured under 1 ms of latency for an uncompressed HDBaseT 3.0 extender, against 40–300 ms for H.265-compressed extenders. That supports using an uncompressed HDBaseT kit such as the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K for gaming, though SC&T did not test that model.

findings.label: Resolutions that worked over a tested Cat6 run (The Gadgeteer, David Sheneman, published 2023-03-05)
findings.value: 3840×2160 at 60p and 24p, plus 1920×1080 at 60p, over about 150 ft (≈46 m) of Cat6
findings.source_title: IOGEAR 4K Video Extender/Splitter Over Ethernet Cable Kit review – The Gadgeteer
findings.note: Laptop source to a TV. The reviewer said the picture was 'as clean and solid as if I had connected it directly to my laptop'. One cable plug had a broken tab and had to be reseated. The 230 ft maximum was not tested. There was slight stutter in 4K Prime Video in Chrome at 60p; the reviewer could not tell whether the extender caused it. Latency was not measured: Sheneman wrote 'Latency wasn't a problem in my testing' and saw at most a very slight cursor delay. IR pass-through from the transmitter end worked.

findings.label: Latency at 4K60 over 100 m of Cat cable (SC&T lab test, published 2026-04-20)
findings.value: HDBaseT 3.0: under 1 ms; SwiftSync (light compression): about 40 ms; H.265 (heavy compression): 40–300 ms
findings.source_title: HDMI Transmission Technology Test Report: HDBaseT 3.0 vs H.265 vs SwiftSync – SC&T Supply
findings.note: Run by SC&T, which makes extenders, using its own HE02U-4K6G (HDBaseT 3.0) and HKM01-4K6G units and an unnamed H.265 extender. A 4K60 PC fed an HDMI splitter into all three, each over 100 m of cable. The outputs were shown side by side with the original source on a quad-view matrix and recorded with a 4K capture box. Latency was compared with a millisecond timer. The report gives no trial count. None of the four candidates was tested, and the OREI kits are HDMI 2.0/HDBaseT 2.0-class rather than HDBaseT 3.0.
